title: StrategySchema
$comment: Compiler output. THE CONTRACT: the engine runs from this and never needs the strategy code. Source: strategy-platform.html + mmarkets.excalidraw.

allOf.$comment: AMENDED (compiler pin): the former triggers-XOR-lifecycle_stages oneOf is gone -- 'triggers' is the always-present document-level trigger table, and 'lifecycle_stages' layers per-leg delivery masks on top; the per-intent index travels with the leg machine (iff both ways: intent ids only exist in the leg-machine vocabulary).

schema_version.$comment: 2 = the compiler-pin shape: document-level triggers, arm-list lifecycle_stages, intent_index, v0.2 envelope.

name.description: Display name from meta.name -- audit/UI context, not an identifier; nothing references it.

dsl_version.description: IR dsl_version the source document conformed to, e.g. '0.2'.

source_hash.description: sha256 (lowercase hex) over the canonical serialization of the validated source document. strategy_id embeds its first 12 hex.

signals.$comment: BREAKING (replaces the former bare-string id list; migration is mechanical: 'btc_mid' -> {signal_id:'btc_mid', staleness_policy:'proceed'}; bump schema_version and coordinate with SME owners -- batch with the condition-tree change, one plumbing release). This object is the subscription ROW -- the first column of the eventual registration bundle. Every future per-subscription fact (payload inclusion, field selection, per-signal dead-bands) lands here additively; the breaking shape change is paid exactly once, now.
signals.description: Per-signal subscription rows: which signals this strategy subscribes to, and what the SME/harness does at activation-assembly time if one is stale. Bound on the feed (signal-definition.staleness_bound), policy on the subscriber (here): two halves of one mechanism.

staleness_policy.description: Checked at activation assembly against the signal's staleness_bound. 'proceed': deliver the last value regardless of age. 'refuse': suppress this activation entirely -- the strategy does not wake; suppression is itself a LOGGED event (strategy, signal, age, bound), so replay reproduces it and 'why didn't my bot fire at 2:14' has an answer of the same quality as 'why did it'. 'degrade': deliver the value with is_stale=true and its age visible in the payload; guards may branch on it (note for Tier 5 layout work: degradable signals grow an is_stale/age field in the payload layout). Age is measured in AVAILABILITY-TIME -- the stamp assigned when the event entered the system -- against the triggering event's availability-time; never venue timestamps (cross-feed skew), never wall clock (nondeterministic under replay). Same clock rule as lazy windows.

watch_fields.description: Specific (signal, field) pairs to record and index.

triggers.$comment: AMENDED (compiler pin): now the ALWAYS-PRESENT document-level trigger table -- one row per trigger, one edge/rearm state, document order; lifecycle_stages (when present) only mask delivery per leg. Absent lifecycle_stages = the flat MVP form (single implicit resident leg arming everything), unchanged.
triggers.description: The document-level trigger table: every trigger the strategy can ever arm, registered once and evaluated continuously for the strategy's whole life. Also the row set a runner forwards into strategy-registration.triggers verbatim.

envelope.$comment: AMENDED (compiler pin): member set replaced with the v0.2 submission envelope, carried verbatim; values are canonical decimal STRINGS -- also fixes the old raw-number violation of the family's decimals-as-strings convention.
envelope.description: The user's risk limits, supplied with the submission (never LLM-authored) and enforced by the risk gate reading THIS -- never the compiled code, which merely inlines the same values as constants. A strategy without an envelope does not load.

allocation.description: Escrowed sub-account capital (USDC); the structural floor.

loss_budget.description: Hard stop via worst-case accounting (USDC): realized loss + open cost basis + resting order notional may never exceed this.

round_budget.$comment: AMENDED (compiler pin, additive): optional per-window budget.
round_budget.description: Per-window budget (USDC): the most one market window may commit -- this window's realized loss + open cost basis + opening notional of resting orders + the next order's opening cost; closing orders are free. Resets with the window. Absent: no per-window cap. At most allocation. Readable from strategy expressions.

max_order_size.description: Per-intent size cap (tokens); the primary magnitude strategies read.

max_exposure_fraction.description: In-flight worst-case exposure fraction of remaining budget. Absent: 1 (no proportional shrinkage). Gate parameter -- not readable from strategy expressions.

pause_at_consumed.description: Fraction of loss budget consumed at which the gate pauses and notifies. Absent: no checkpoint. Gate parameter -- not readable from strategy expressions.

max_open_orders.description: Maker book-footprint cap (count). Absent: venue default.

state_layout.$comment: Per-kind requirements (key_types/max_keys iff map; entry_type/capacity iff window; value_type vs value_window mutually exclusive on map) are enforced by the validator / shared crate, NOT by schema conditionals -- five interlocking if/thens across three kinds is gymnastics, and the crate's Rust enums make the invalid states unconstructible (Kind::Map { key_types, max_keys } cannot even be built wrong). This is a live argument for the shared crate: the schema file is the weaker representation here. THE ALGEBRA'S CEILING, deliberate (like DNF for triggers): containers hold primitives or structs; ONE nesting level exists -- map-of-windows ('last 5 shots per player' = map<player, window<shot,5>>, allocation = max_keys x capacity x entry_size, bounded x bounded = bounded). No maps of maps, no structs of structs, no deeper nesting: full recursion makes layout, cost stamping, and the English decompilation arbitrarily hard for expressiveness no corpus strategy demanded. CLAIM: any bounded state decomposes into scalar | map | window over primitives-or-structs with map-of-windows as the one nesting; a strategy that does not fit is a design conversation, not a schema tweak -- 'I cannot state my bound' has so far always meant 'I am actually a signal' (signal-layer work: platform time-series processor or private feed, and the strategy triggers on the resulting number). Absent state_layout = stateless strategy.
state_layout.description: Allocation contract: every memory slot this strategy owns. The harness allocates from this list; the compiled code addresses these slots. NO update logic here -- folds, resets, and sets are compiled into the executable; this section only answers 'how much memory, shaped how'. Map overflow policy (refuse-update vs evict) is IR-side, baked into the executable and disclosed in the decompilation -- the harness needs only the size; do not add a policy enum here. Byte offsets deliberately absent for the name-keyed era; when offsets arrive they are ADDED here (manifest owns layout) -- consumers must not assume this list is the final layout authority yet.

region.description: strategy: written by compiled code (via set/folds), read/write. platform: written ONLY by the harness from exchange lifecycle events (position, entry fill price/qty, realized PnL); READ-ONLY to strategy code. The compiler declares platform slots so cross-leg references ('entry price x 1.02') have an allocated home; the harness enforces the write boundary -- a compiled artifact whose writes touch a platform slot is refused (validator check; this field is what makes it checkable).

value_type.description: scalar: the slot's type. map: the value type per key (mutually exclusive with value_window).

key_types.description: map only: the key tuple's component types, e.g. [u8, u8] for (team, quarter). Needed to size an entry.

max_keys.description: map only: hard capacity, fixed at compile time. Allocation = max_keys x entry size. REQUIRED for kind=map (validator-enforced).

capacity.description: window only: max retained entries. Overflow is drop-oldest, fixed platform-wide (the behavioral consequence -- a by-age window may undercount in a burst -- is disclosed in the decompilation, not configured here). REQUIRED for kind=window (validator-enforced).

entry_type.description: window only: type of each retained entry -- a primitive or a struct ((price, size) together).

value_window.description: map only, THE one permitted nesting: each map value is itself a window (map-of-windows). Mutually exclusive with value_type (validator-enforced). Allocation = max_keys x capacity x entry size.

offset.description: RESERVED, name-keyed era: absent. Compiler-assigned byte offset within the state block when layouts go physical.

slot_bytes.description: Compiler-computed size of this slot: scalars by type; maps = max_keys x (key tuple + value); windows = capacity x entry + ring bookkeeping. Present NOW even in the name-keyed era -- it feeds the cost stamp and admission math, and it's how the decompilation can say 'this strategy uses 2.1 KB of memory'. Sizes don't constrain the runtime representation; offsets ARE the runtime representation, which is why slot_bytes ships now and offset stays reserved.

layout_hash.description: Hex hash of the canonicalized layout-relevant sections: payload_layouts, state_layout (with sizes), scratch_bytes, max_intents_per_activation -- same canonicalization discipline as signal-id.md (sorted keys, canonical numbers; one hashing implementation in the shared crate, two users). Deliberately EXCLUDED: envelope, triggers, cost stamp -- behavioral facts, not layout facts; changing a cooldown must not invalidate resident activations. Stamped on every activation; the harness refuses mismatches -- a strategy compiled in March resident in July under a redeployed SME gets a loud refusal and an alert, never a name-keyed silent misread or a byte-offset garbage-read-traded-on.

scratch_bytes.description: Worst-case ephemeral space for expression evaluation across ALL legs (fixed-depth stack; iterative builtins at compiler-computed worst case). Harness-allocated once, zeroed per activation, invisible to the author. Computable exactly BECAUSE the language has no loops or allocation -- this field existing is the proof that 'runtime allocation does not exist' is enforceable rather than aspirational.

max_intents_per_activation.description: Countable at compile time: the largest number of intents any single activation can emit (max over legs of intents reachable in one firing). The harness preallocates the output buffer to this; the compiled function writes into it and CANNOT overflow it, because emitting more than this many intents is unexpressible in the language.

total_state_bytes.description: Sum of all state_layout slot_bytes, including platform-region slots. The harness's single allocation number (one alloc(total) instead of per-slot bookkeeping); the admission controller's memory input. Validator: must equal the sum of the declared slot_bytes.

payload_layouts.$comment: VALIDATOR RULES (shared crate): every key names a declared leg (for the flat-trigger form, the single implicit leg's layout is keyed by the reserved name 'main'); every (signal_id, field) references a subscribed signal at its declared version; staleness_meta=true only where the subscription's staleness_policy is 'degrade'.
payload_layouts.description: Per-leg activation payload contract, keyed by leg name. The SME assembles each activation in EXACTLY this order with exactly these entries -- the full declared context, not just the field that flipped -- and compiled code reads assuming it; the manifest is what keeps assembler and reader agreeing without ever talking. Per-leg because legs need different signal sets (the quoter's management leg wants inventory and vol; the hunting leg doesn't) and shipping the union to every activation is waste that grows with strategy complexity. NAME-KEYED ERA: entries are matched by (signal_id, field) name; 'offset' is absent. When byte-offset payloads arrive, offsets are ADDED to these entries and the list order becomes physical order -- consumers must already treat this list as the layout authority, not the dict's key set.

staleness_meta.description: true when this subscription's policy is 'degrade': the payload carries is_stale + age_ms alongside the value. This is Tier 2's degrade consequence, landing exactly where predicted.

offset.description: RESERVED for the byte-offset era. Absent = name-keyed. Present in the schema now so no consumer builds assume-it's-always-a-dict code that would make the migration painful.

lifecycle_stages.$comment: AMENDED (compiler pin): rules/transitions/partial_fill_policy/on_exit_orders deleted -- trigger state is document-level and continuous (see 'triggers'), so a stage is just a named delivery mask ('arm'); order-outcome transitions moved to the per-intent index ('intent_index'). Fresh-on-leg-entry registration semantics are gone: arming and disarming never register, reset, or rewind trigger bookkeeping (timers excepted -- per-arming by ratified IR semantics).
lifecycle_stages.description: The leg machine. Exactly one leg is active at a time; the initial leg is the first array element. 'arm' lists which document-level triggers are DELIVERED while the leg is active -- a mask, nothing more. Guards, bodies, and intents live in the compiled artifact.

name.description: Unique leg name; 'stay' is reserved and may not be used.

resident.description: true: this leg may legitimately never exit and is exempt from the liveness check. false: the validator requires at least one path out.

arm.description: Ids of the document-level triggers delivered while this leg is active. Empty = a terminal leg that wakes for nothing. Every id names an entry in 'triggers' (validator rule).

intent_index.$comment: NEW (compiler pin): per-intent totalized transition tables + bounds, replacing the per-leg transitions machinery. Executed mechanically by the runner (no strategy code runs on order events) and snapshotted onto each order at placement, so tables survive later leg changes. 'stay'-or-declared-leg-name on destinations is a validator rule -- the schema cannot see the leg set.
intent_index.description: intent_id -> transition table and bounds. intent_id is '<leg>.<block>.<do-index>' -- the validator-diagnostic path vocabulary; an opaque key plus provenance, never parsed for semantics.

DecimalString.description: Canonical unsigned decimal string: no exponents, no leading '+', no leading/trailing dot, no leading zeros on the integer part, no trailing fractional zeros.

IntentEntry.$comment: The five-key alphabet is PINNED without 'replaced' -- v0.2's ratified order-event alphabet; if AJ's cancel_replace-ack answer keeps 'replaced' in common.OrderEvent, this table gains the key (compiler totalizes it to 'stay') in the same commit.

on.description: TOTAL transition table: every key present, defaults materialized as 'stay', never implied. Each value is 'stay' or a declared leg name (validator rule).

max_size.description: Resolved per-intent size bound -- the risk path enforces this without trusting the code's arithmetic.
